messages.text: `sh` is not available in this PowerShell-only environment, so deleting `./executable` made local wrapper validation weaker. I’m restoring a POSIX `./executable` alongside the Windows `./executable.cmd`, then verifying the actual Python entrypoints and differential behavior again; the `compile.sh` content remains a POSIX build script for the evaluator.

commands.preview: Get-Content -Raw compile.sh; Get-ChildItem -Force executable,executable.cmd,zip_password_finder.py,compile.sh | Select-Object Name,Length,Mode | Format-Table -AutoSize
commands.receipt:
#!/usr/bin/env sh
set -eu
if [ ! -f executable ]; then
  cp zip_password_finder.py executable
fi
chmod +x executable 2>/dev/null || true
if [ -n "${OS:-}" ] && [ "$OS" = "Windows_NT" ]; then
  [ -f executable.cmd ]
else
  [ -f executable ]
fi
